complexity.correctness_reason: Relies on float division for comparing arrival times, which is provably safe only because NeetCode caps target and speed at 10^6 (minimum distinct-time gap ~1e-12 stays well above rounding error); once the caps are lifted, e.g. target near 10^10 with times like 9999990001/999999 vs 10000000001/1000000 differing by ~1e-12, both quotients can round to the same double and flip a fleet decision.
complexity.notes: The print() call is leftover debugging: it computes math.ceil values that are never used and adds O(n) I/O per run — delete it. List is not imported; harmless since CPython 3.14 defers annotation evaluation (PEP 649), but `from typing import List` would be tidier. The float division for arrival times is the only fragile part: comparing times with ||exact integer cross-multiplication, (target-p1)*s2 vs (target-p2)*s1|| would remove all precision concerns. Sorted order could also be produced without the full pairwise list via ||zip(position, speed) sorted by position||, which is purely cosmetic.
complexity.summary: Sorts cars by position and scans from the car nearest the target backward, merging a car into the fleet ahead whenever its float arrival time is at most the lead car's and counting a new fleet otherwise.
